articles.title: Surveillance and control efficacy of the Bergerac, France, 2025 chikungunya outbreak

en.research_question: How effectively did varying intensities and geographic scopes of vector control interventions influence the trajectory of a chikungunya outbreak in a French municipality?
en.study_design: The investigation utilized a climate-informed mathematical framework to simulate mosquito-borne virus transmission and compared simulated outputs against observed epidemiological records.
en.population_setting: The analysis focused on a 2025 chikungunya cluster in Bergerac, France, which emerged following introductions linked to international travel from an affected overseas territory.
en.main_findings: Early interventions restricted in scope and intensity demonstrated minimal capacity to curb transmission during periods of rapid viral spread. Conversely, expanded operational efforts alongside heightened community vigilance corresponded with a marked decline in reported infections.
en.public_health_relevance: The results indicate that aligning intervention magnitude with transmission severity and sustaining continuous monitoring are essential strategies for managing emerging arboviral threats in temperate regions.
en.gids_interpretation: This work contributes to the literature on computational approaches for forecasting arbovirus dynamics under changing environmental conditions. It provides methodological context for evaluating how response timing and resource allocation influence outbreak trajectories without implying current real-time monitoring status.

articles.title: A Systematic Review of New, Enhanced Surveillance Systems and Methodologies for Zoonotic Influenza Viruses in Animals and Human-Animal Interface.

diseases.name_zh: 人感染高致病性禽流感

en.research_question: The authors aimed to evaluate recent developments in monitoring techniques for animal and cross-species influenza viruses to determine which innovations warrant broader application and which areas require further investigation.
en.study_design: This work follows a systematic review framework guided by PRISMA standards, synthesizing data from 164 selected publications out of an initial search yielding 7,490 records.
en.population_setting: The scope encompasses global efforts to track influenza strains circulating among wildlife, livestock, and humans, with particular attention to interaction zones where spillover events occur.
en.main_findings: The analysis identifies multiple technological improvements alongside persistent structural deficiencies in monitoring networks. Current documentation indicates that numerous regions operate without robust cross-sectoral tracking systems, resulting in incomplete estimates of infection prevalence. Priority actions emphasize integrating multi-sectoral datasets, standardizing new testing tools, scaling passive sampling strategies, and aligning technical upgrades with regulatory decision-making.
en.public_health_relevance: Strengthening coordinated monitoring frameworks is presented as essential for reducing seasonal illness impacts and mitigating future outbreak threats through improved diagnostic readiness and targeted research funding.
en.limitations: The evaluation relies exclusively on indexed academic publications, which may overlook operational field data or reflect uneven research investment across different geographic areas. Additionally, the focus on a seven-year window restricts historical context for long-term trend analysis.
en.gids_interpretation: This publication offers a consolidated perspective on methodological evolution within cross-species pathogen tracking initiatives. It contextualizes recent scholarly contributions toward standardized data collection and policy alignment without referencing active epidemiological dashboards or real-time transmission metrics.

articles.title: Resurgent threat in a changing climate: A 20-year bibliometric analysis of global Chikungunya research evolution and pandemic preparedness

en.research_question: Maps two decades of global scientific output to determine current priorities and unmet needs in chikungunya pandemic readiness.
en.study_design: Bibliometric evaluation of 8,125 indexed articles published between 2004 and 2025, utilizing software tools to track citation trends, author networks, and keyword co-occurrence patterns.
en.population_setting: Global scientific literature and publishing records rather than a defined clinical or demographic cohort.
en.main_findings: Article production expanded sevenfold following 2013, coinciding with major regional outbreaks. Research activity concentrated within four primary national hubs. Scholarly focus has progressively shifted toward immunization development and environmental transmission factors, while diagnostic differentiation and crisis management keywords have diminished in frequency.
en.public_health_relevance: Highlights increasing academic investment in vaccine platforms and climate-linked transmission models. Identifies structural imbalances in multinational research partnerships and recommends aligning pathogen readiness initiatives with broader environmental health planning.
en.limitations: Analysis depends entirely on database-indexed publications, potentially overlooking non-traditional or regionally restricted research outputs. The methodology quantifies scholarly productivity and thematic shifts rather than measuring actual disease incidence or intervention effectiveness.
en.gids_interpretation: Functions as a retrospective mapping of academic publishing trends instead of an active monitoring report. Offers context on how research emphasis has evolved toward preventive technologies and ecological drivers without generating new empirical signal data.

zh.research_question: 瑞典户外职业人群对蜱传脑炎的疫苗接种覆盖率及其相关知识、态度与行为现状如何？
zh.study_design: 该研究采用全国性横断面调查设计，于二零二四年收集数据以评估目标人群的免疫实践状况。
zh.population_setting: 研究对象为瑞典从事农业、林业、狩猎、科研及自然导览等户外作业成年人员。
zh.main_findings: 受访者对疫苗的认知与态度整体处于中等偏上水平，但实际接种率未能同步提升且存在显著差异。女性群体及南部和中部地区居民的参与比例较高，约七成报告已完成至少三剂接种，但部分细分人群中仍存在未接种现象。
zh.public_health_relevance: 尽管高危职业群体具备一定疾病防范意识，但免疫屏障尚未完全建立，提示需通过定向干预与政策优化来缩小接种缺口。
zh.limitations: 作为基于单一时间点的横断面自我报告调查，该设计难以确立变量间的时序关系，且可能受到回忆偏差的影响。
zh.gids_interpretation: 本文提供了瑞典特定职业暴露背景下的免疫模式基线信息，可作为区域健康监测框架的背景参考，不涉及实时疫情信号关联。

en.research_question: The investigation aimed to quantify tick-borne encephalitis immunization rates among Swedish individuals employed in outdoor occupations, addressing a documented gap in existing epidemiological data.
en.study_design: Researchers utilized a nationwide cross-sectional survey methodology to collect self-reported knowledge, attitudes, and practice data during 2024.
en.population_setting: The analytical sample comprised 1006 consenting adults working in outdoor sectors such as agriculture, forestry, hunting, scientific research, and wildlife guiding across Sweden.
en.main_findings: Participants exhibited moderate awareness and positive views regarding immunization, yet actual uptake rates fell short of these metrics and differed markedly across demographics. Female respondents achieved higher assessment scores and vaccination rates than males, while geographic analysis revealed superior coverage in southern and central counties relative to northern areas. Roughly seventy percent indicated completion of a three-dose regimen, although distinct demographic clusters remained largely unprotected.
en.public_health_relevance: Rising regional disease incidence contrasts with the exclusion of the prophylactic agent from official immunization schedules, highlighting the need for occupational-specific interventions and financial support mechanisms to mitigate transmission risk.
en.limitations: The cross-sectional framework restricts temporal analysis of behavioral shifts, and reliance on self-reported immunization records introduces potential recall inaccuracies.
en.gids_interpretation: This publication establishes a descriptive baseline for occupational immunization patterns, offering contextual reference points for literature mapping and regional health strategy discussions without implying real-time outbreak tracking.

zh.research_question: 本研究旨在评估2024年全球登革热的整体疾病负担，并探讨影响各国登革热相关死亡率的潜在关联因素。
zh.study_design: 该研究采用观察性生态分析设计，提取世界卫生组织全球监测系统提供的2024年1月至12月月度汇总数据，并应用广义线性回归模型进行多变量关联检验。
zh.population_setting: 研究覆盖全球范围，主要依赖各国向国际机构上报的汇总数据，分析焦点涵盖南半球区域以及具有不同年龄结构与气候特征的国家群体。
zh.main_findings: 2024年全球累计报告病例约一千四百一十万例，死亡九千五百零八例，总体病死率为百分之零点零七。回归分析表明，南半球地理位置、较高的人口老龄化水平以及较高的年均气温，均与国家层面每百万人口的登革热死亡率呈显著正相关。
zh.public_health_relevance: 研究指出登革热传播规模持续扩大已构成严峻的公共卫生压力，呼吁国际社会加大对病毒学基础科研、疫苗与药物研发、病媒生物防控及临床干预方案的资源倾斜，并建议将其列入优先研发疾病清单。
zh.limitations: 分析完全基于各国上报的宏观汇总数据，缺乏个体患者层面的临床信息，且未对各国监测报告体系的完整性与时效性差异进行量化校正。
zh.gids_interpretation: 该文献通过历史年度数据的回顾性梳理，呈现了登革热流行规模的演变轨迹及其与地理、人口和气象指标的统计学联系，为后续趋势追踪提供基线参考，不涉及实时疫情预警或现场流调结论。

articles.title: Salmonellosis Outbreak in a Rottweiler Kennel Associated with Raw Meat-Based Diets

en.research_question: To characterize the clinical presentation, microbiological profile, and environmental spread of a Salmonella infection within a canine breeding facility.
en.study_design: A descriptive case report and outbreak investigation utilizing clinical observation, sample collection, and laboratory diagnostics.
en.population_setting: A Bulgarian Rottweiler breeding kennel comprising adult and post-partum dogs.
en.main_findings: Affected animals exhibited gastrointestinal symptoms and lethargy, with more severe presentations occurring in recently whelped females. Microbiological testing revealed extensive bacterial shedding among the dogs alongside contamination of their diet and surrounding surfaces. Full recovery followed the cessation of raw diet administration, implementation of targeted drug therapy, and thorough sanitation, while exposed humans remained uninfected.
en.public_health_relevance: The report highlights the cross-species transmission potential of pathogens found in unregulated raw animal feed. It advocates for enhanced feed traceability and biosecurity standards to mitigate health threats under a collaborative veterinary-human health approach.
en.limitations: The evaluation relies on observational data from a single facility without a comparative control cohort. Consequently, the observed outcomes may not reflect broader canine populations or different regional conditions.
en.gids_interpretation: This article contributes to the academic record of veterinary infectious disease events and diagnostic methodologies. Its documentation aids scholarly monitoring of dietary-related microbial risks in domestic animal settings.

articles.title: A Case-Control Study on the Effectiveness of Tick-Borne Encephalitis Vaccination Against Hospitalizations in an Endemic Area in Northeastern Italy.

en.research_question: What is the protective impact of the tick-borne encephalitis immunization regimen in preventing severe disease requiring medical admission among residents of a recognized endemic zone in northeastern Italy?
en.study_design: The investigation employed a case-control methodology utilizing linked regional health records spanning seven years. Participants were stratified based on hospitalization status following laboratory confirmation of infection.
en.population_setting: The analysis focused on inhabitants of the Udine province within the Friuli Venezia Giulia region, which is classified as an endemic zone for the pathogen.
en.main_findings: Individuals receiving three or more vaccine doses demonstrated a substantially reduced likelihood of hospital admission compared to those without immunization. Provincial coverage reached approximately ten percent, with notably higher rates recorded in elevated geographic districts.
en.public_health_relevance: The documentation underscores the value of immunization strategies in reducing severe disease outcomes within affected communities. Regional variations in coverage indicate opportunities for targeted outreach initiatives to improve community protection.
en.limitations: The evaluation was constrained by a limited number of confirmed hospitalization events.
en.gids_interpretation: This publication offers background information on regional immunization practices and documented protection levels against severe neurological infections. It serves as a reference point for understanding historical prevention efforts rather than indicating current outbreak dynamics.

articles.title: Transmission pathways and risk factors for sporadic salmonellosis and campylobacteriosis: a source attribution meta-analysis of European case-control studies.

en.research_question: What are the primary transmission routes and attributable sources for sporadic campylobacteriosis and salmonellosis across European populations?
en.study_design: A Bayesian meta-analytical framework was utilized to combine population attributable fractions extracted from multiple European case-control investigations spanning two decades.
en.population_setting: Participants comprised individuals diagnosed with sporadic infections alongside matched controls recruited from Western and Northern European healthcare settings.
en.main_findings: Dietary and aquatic exposures accounted for nearly fifty percent of infections, with poultry products representing the dominant reservoir for Campylobacter and both poultry and pork contributing substantially to Salmonella cases. Incorporating direct animal interactions raised the zoonotic contribution to approximately sixty percent, while environmental factors explained roughly ten percent. The remaining portion of cases correlated with international travel, preexisting medical conditions, pharmaceutical interventions, interpersonal contact, and workplace activities.
en.public_health_relevance: Identifying dominant reservoirs and exposure routes supports targeted prevention strategies and resource allocation for enteric pathogen control across European health systems.
en.limitations: The synthesis relies exclusively on aggregated data from previously published case-control investigations, which may introduce variability in how exposure categories were defined and reported across different regions.
en.gids_interpretation: This publication offers a synthesized overview of historical attribution patterns for two major bacterial enteritides, serving as a reference point for transmission ecology rather than reflecting active outbreak detection or real-time epidemiological tracking.

articles.title: Transmission Pathways of Zoonotic Influenza Viruses and Influencing Factors: A Systematic Review of Recent Findings.

en.research_question: This systematic review synthesizes recent literature to identify how zoonotic influenza viruses move between animal populations and spill over into human communities, alongside the variables that facilitate these cross-species transfers.
en.study_design: The authors conducted a systematic review adhering to PRISMA standards, screening thousands of database records to select relevant publications spanning seven years.
en.population_setting: The analysis encompasses studies involving wild and domestic animal reservoirs, as well as human populations affected by cross-species viral transfer, without restricting geographic boundaries.
en.main_findings: The synthesis highlights existing knowledge on host, environmental, and viral drivers of transmission while revealing substantial unexplored areas regarding interspecies movement, ecological influences, and regional zoonotic risks.
en.public_health_relevance: Clarifying these transmission mechanisms supports improved pandemic preparedness and underscores the importance of coordinated, multi-sectoral health frameworks to mitigate future spillover threats.
en.limitations: The authors acknowledge that the reviewed corpus contains notable gaps, specifically regarding viral circulation across varied animal hosts, the precise influence of ecological variables, and regional variations in cross-species risk.
en.gids_interpretation: This work situates ongoing academic inquiry into viral ecology within established international research priorities, offering a consolidated reference point for scholars tracking cross-species pathogen movement.

zh.research_question: 本研究旨在系统梳理2017年至2024年间关于人畜共患流感病毒传播途径及相关影响因素的文献，以明确跨物种传播的关键机制。
zh.study_design: 该研究遵循PRISMA指南开展系统评价，从PubMed初筛的7490篇记录中严格筛选出219篇文献进行综合分析。
zh.population_setting: 研究聚焦于野生与家养动物群体中的流感病毒传播，以及病毒跨越物种屏障感染人类的潜在过程。
zh.main_findings: 综述归纳了宿主行为、生态环境与病毒特性共同作用于传播网络的现有证据。分析表明，当前在复杂动物间传播链、环境变量量化影响及跨区域人畜共患风险图谱方面仍缺乏充分数据。
zh.public_health_relevance: 完善上述知识缺口有助于制定更精准的防控预案，并推动将多部门协同的健康管理框架纳入公共卫生规划。
zh.limitations: 作者直接指出，现有文献在阐明多样化动物宿主间的传播规律、解析环境因子的独立作用以及评估不同地域的跨种感染可能性上存在明显局限。
zh.gids_interpretation: 该文献系统整理了近年来的学术探讨，为理解人畜共患流感的传播机制演变提供了背景脉络，适合作为领域知识检索与主题定位的参考资料。

articles.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

related_surveillance.method: high-confidence article geography intersected with GIDS series coverage
high-confidence article geography intersected with GIDS series coverage

en.research_question: The study seeks to identify environmental and demographic drivers associated with human H7N9 infections and to map historical risk zones across China.
en.study_design: Researchers applied a MaxEnt computational framework to analyze case locations alongside environmental and socioeconomic datasets spanning five years.
en.population_setting: The analysis focused on human cases reported throughout China, with particular attention to coastal provinces during the 2013 through 2017 timeframe.
en.main_findings: Model outputs indicate a steady annual escalation in infection probability, consistently highlighting eastern and southeastern coastal regions as persistent hotspots. Demographic concentration served as the strongest predictor, while ecological and agricultural metrics provided secondary explanatory power. Simulated risk distributions demonstrated strong agreement with documented outbreak locations.
en.public_health_relevance: Mapping these spatial trends and variable contributions may help guide resource allocation for targeted monitoring and intervention planning.
en.limitations: The authors acknowledge that expanding the dataset with additional variables is necessary to enhance predictive precision and strengthen policy guidance.
en.gids_interpretation: This work functions as a retrospective geospatial assessment that contextualizes historical H7N9 distribution patterns and their associated correlates, rather than providing an active monitoring mechanism.

zh.research_question: 本研究旨在探讨中国人群感染禽流感A(H7N9)病毒的相关影响因素及其传播特征，并评估潜在的高风险地理区域。
zh.study_design: 该研究采用MaxEnt算法进行回顾性空间建模，利用2013至2017年的病例点位与环境及社会经济数据进行相关性检验。
zh.population_setting: 研究聚焦于中国境内报告过H7N9确诊病例的地理范围，时间跨度覆盖2013年至2017年。
zh.main_findings: 模型模拟显示疫情风险呈逐年上升态势，东部与东南部沿海地带持续处于高风险区间。人口密度被识别为核心关联变量，植被覆盖、降水、海拔、家禽屠宰规模、产值及气温等亦为次要相关因素。模拟生成的风险分布图与实际疫情记录高度吻合。
zh.public_health_relevance: 明确关键关联变量与高风险地理分布可为公共卫生部门优化监测网络布局及资源配置提供科学参考。
zh.limitations: 作者明确指出当前模型纳入的变量集较为有限，未来需补充更多参数以提升预测精度并增强对防控策略的指导价值。
zh.gids_interpretation: 该文提供的是基于历史数据的回顾性空间风险评估背景信息，侧重于环境与社会经济变量的关联性分析，未涉及实时监测信号的直接验证或前瞻性预警。

articles.title: Seasonal Mathematical Model of Salmonellosis Transmission and the Role of Contaminated Environments and Food Products

zh.research_question: 本研究旨在构建数学模型，以探究沙门氏菌在人类、牲畜及受污染环境中的季节性传播动态，并识别决定疾病持续或消亡的关键参数。
zh.study_design: 该研究采用非自主数学建模方法，结合拉丁超立方抽样与最小二乘法对历史暴发数据进行参数校准，并利用谱半径理论推导基本再生数及阈值条件。
zh.population_setting: 模型包含人类、牛群以及环境与食品源中的细菌群体，参数估计基于沙特阿拉伯2018至2021年间的沙门氏菌暴发记录。
zh.main_findings: 估算的基本再生数为0.606，模型对累计与新发病例数据的拟合度较高，提示疾病具备可控潜力。模拟表明当再生数低于1时疾病趋于消亡，高于1时则呈现地方性流行特征。敏感性分析指出死亡率、感染率及衰减率对传播结果具有决定性影响。
zh.public_health_relevance: 该计算框架通过量化不同传播路径与关键参数的作用，为解析沙门氏菌的传播机制提供了理论依据，有助于评估各类干预策略对改变传播阈值的潜在贡献。
zh.limitations: 研究性质为理论推演与数值模拟，其结论高度依赖单一区域的历史数据输入及预设的种群假设，尚未纳入实地验证或复杂的社会行为变量。
zh.gids_interpretation: 作为计算流行病学文献，该成果侧重于揭示季节波动与环境媒介对传播网络的结构化影响，可为相关监测体系的理论参数设定提供学术参考，但不构成对当前实时疫情态势的直接印证。
